implementation_notes: Nest builds its route from DI metadata: registering the audit interceptor as an APP_INTERCEPTOR provider inside a conditional spread - or applying @UseInterceptors(AuditInterceptor) to one controller - is the toggle, and the interceptor's next.handle() call is the rejoin to the same handler. The same code without DI is a typed Express middleware chain mounted conditionally. Keeping the interceptor's RxJS pipeline observational (tap-style) is what keeps the enabled and disabled legs equivalent.
pitfalls: An APP_INTERCEPTOR provider is global regardless of the module that declares it; use @UseInterceptors for a method- or controller-scoped toggle.
An interceptor that does not call next.handle() replaces the handler's result (stream overriding), so a caching detour can silently bypass the destination.
Interceptors do not apply to the library-specific response strategy (@Res()), so mixing the two makes the detour appear to do nothing.
